stationComplexesNote: The inverse of stationSplitExceptions. That table forgives ONE package station id whose platforms are further apart than the band allows; this one names the case where ONE physical station complex arrived as SEVERAL package station ids, because no two of its operators share a stop vocabulary and group_stations' 140 m name-blind / 400 m same-name rules could not reach across the concourse. Washington Union Station arrives as three ids 280 m apart and no anchor sees more than three of the seven railways that call there. Each entry is keyed by the group code that survives; every code in `absorbs` is rewritten to that key, and ONLY for a platform whose own coordinate is within `maxMeters` of `center`. The centre/radius test is what keeps a slug collision out: `us-official-penn` holds both LIRR's platforms at New York Penn and NJ Transit's Newark Light Rail platform 14.4 km away, and only the first is inside the New York circle. A complex carries TRANSFER semantics and nothing else. It assigns a station code and, where `name` is given, the one name the place is called by. It reads coordinates and never writes one: no anchor moves, no centroid is computed, no railway is pulled onto another's alignment, and each line keeps its own station slot on its own geometry -- which is exactly what rail-network.js already does with the code it is given, counting railways per group for the hollow interchange mark and electing one platform per group to carry the label. Same name and nearby does NOT make one complex: two TTC streetcar stops on opposite corners of an intersection are two stops, so every entry names its own evidence. The GTFS feed hashes the stationSplitExceptions entries carry are not available for entries added after the North America source tree was purged; `packageEvidence` is the substitute -- a measurement any reader can reproduce from the shipped package alone.

reviewedStraightIntervalsNote: A straight station interval on a line drawn from an audited OpenStreetMap relation, looked at one at a time. The relation is accepted as the alignment only because the registry can show it was validated against an independent government survey, and record_audited_relation_straights measures each straight interval against the relation's own geometry before recording it; this table is the annotation on that record, for the interval where the relation carries no interior node and only a worst-case bound can be stated. It is not a way past the measurement: an interval whose relation slice is not straight is refused whether or not it appears here. Keyed by package line id, then by the ordered station pair, so a folded or renumbered interval cannot inherit someone else's review.

ttc-2.why: OSM relation 102386 draws Woodbine to Main Street as a single straight way with no interior node on either running track, so the relation states the track is straight here but carries no vertex that measures it; the reviewed worst-case sagitta consistent with the mapped geometry at either end is 2.23 m, above the 1.5 m the public audit treats as straight, so the interval is recorded as a reviewed exception rather than as a measured one. The City of Toronto topographic subway-track survey COTGEO_TOPO_RAILWAY subtype 2005 does not reach this section, which is in tunnel. Reviewed 2026-09-05.

Stop 20965 (called by B1/B2/B3 trips) and stop 841 (called only by bus routes 28/57/70/B1_OWL) publish the identical name 'Fern Rock Transit Center' 21 m apart, so the default same-name merge already folds them into one station; listing 20965 first keeps the merged station's coordinate on the rail platform (about 59 m from the surveyed septa-b1/b3 Fern Rock terminal vertex) instead of the unrelated bus stop, which the same merge would otherwise apply to every B1/B2/B3 trip calling at Fern Rock. At Norristown Transit Center route M1 calls at stop 30520 (parent_station 31038) and at stop 32185 (no parent_station), 8.2 m apart, both published as 'Norristown Transit Center' and both 22.5-33.3 m from parent 31038; 32185 became us-official-norristown-2, and because it was a station the trunk lacked, the M1 pattern running over it survived drop_subsets as the branch septa-m1-b2. Both groups list SEPTA's own location_type=1 station id first so the surviving station keeps the coordinate the operator declares for the station rather than a platform's or the bus stop's; 30332 is deliberately left out, because no rail route calls there. feeds.stationIdentityEvidence: TTC official GTFS publishes no parent_station and no location_type on any of its 9,402 stops, so station identity has to be rebuilt from stop names, and canonical_feed_parents merges two same-name stops only when the newcomer is within 200 m of EVERY stop already in the cluster. Two things defeat that here. (1) At Cedarvale, Dundas West, Eglinton, High Park, Leslie, Royal York, Sheppard-Yonge and York Mills the station's bus bays are published under the bare station name (ten stops called 'York Mills Station', eight called 'Cedarvale Station'), so the name cluster is seeded by a bus terminal that is itself 50-150 m across; the second rail platform is only 130-147 m from the nearest member of that cluster but 208-241 m from its far side, and the all-pairs test rejects it -- 'York Mills Station - Southbound Platform' (13792) is 134.4 m from 'York Mills Station - Northbound Platform' (13791) but 236.3 m from bus bay 14810, and 'Sheppard-Yonge Station - Southbound Platform' (13860) is 129.6 m from the nearest member of the 14771 cluster and 218.6 m from its farthest. (2) Line 5's two surface pairs, 'Golden Mile Station Eastbound Platform'/'Golden Mile Station Westbound Platform' (16085/16086, 211.4 m) and 'Hakimi Lebovic Station Eastbound Platform'/'Hakimi Lebovic Station Westbound Platform' (16226/16227, 208.3 m), straddle a wide intersection and simply exceed 200 m with no bus stop involved. Either way one physical station arrived as two package station ids, and because the second id was a station the trunk lacked, the short-turn stopping patterns that run over the opposite platform survived drop_subsets as branches: ttc-1-b1 (North York Centre to Davisville, 7.85 km), ttc-2-b1 (Islington to Old Mill), ttc-2-b2 (Runnymede to Lansdowne), ttc-4-b1 and ttc-4-b2 -- Line 4 has no branches at all, its five stations are all on the trunk -- plus ttc-5-b1 and ttc-5-b2; seven strokes redrawing track the trunk already draws. Every group below lists only platforms the TTC itself names for one station, and the first id in each group is the platform the trunk pattern already anchors on, so the surviving station keeps its coordinate and only the duplicate disappears. Sheppard-Yonge additionally folds the Line 4 platforms 13861/13862 ('Sheppard-Yonge Station - Subway Platform', 'Sheppard-Yonge Station - Eastbound Platform', 152.4 m across the group), Eglinton the Line 5 platforms 16073/16074 and Cedarvale the Line 5 platforms 16069/16070, all published under the same station name within 215 m. Three further same-name TTC pairs are deliberately NOT listed and remain separate package stations pending review: Spadina (Line 1 platforms 13853/13854 vs Line 2 platforms 13851/13852, 202-369 m apart), Finch West (Line 1 15658/15659 vs 'Finch West Station LRT Platform' 16323/16324, 154-247 m), and the two stops both called 'Gerrard St East at Coxwell Ave' (1085 and 1117, 322 m apart on different legs of the Coxwell junction), which are two streetcar stops and not one station.
